source_refs.note: Chapter 3 exercise (PDF 47-48) with the answer key (PDF 48, printed 44); every key entry matches the text.

blocks.text: The chapter exercise has ten multiple choice questions, ten short questions and eight long questions. The short and long questions are answered in the lessons of topics 3.1 and 3.2.

blocks.caption: Multiple choice answers
rows: 1 The OOP concept that hides data inside a class
(c) encapsulation
2 Classes and objects are best described as
(b) classes are blueprints and objects are their instances
3 The main idea behind encapsulation
(a) hide data inside a class and prevent unauthorised access
4 Inheritance means
(a) reusing and extending functionality from a parent class to a child class
5 Polymorphism is best defined as
(a) allowing an object to take multiple forms through method overriding
6 An example of inheritance in Python
(b) a child class inheriting attributes and methods from a parent class
7 The purpose of polymorphism
(b) allow a function or method to have different implementations
8 The keyword that defines a class in Python
(b) class
9 Encapsulation is best described as
(a) combining data and methods into one unit and controlling access to the data
10 Inheritance allows a class to
(b) inherit attributes and methods from another class

items: Short 1: topic 3.1. Short 2-4 (class, class versus object, __init__): topic 3.2, classes and objects. Short 5-6: topic 3.2, encapsulation. Short 7-8: topic 3.2, inheritance. Short 9-10: topic 3.2, polymorphism.
Long 1 and 8: classes and objects. Long 2 and 6: encapsulation. Long 3 and 4: inheritance. Long 5: polymorphism. Long 7: the last check question of topic 3.2.
